items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: And I went to see Arturo live. And he goes, “Frank, what are you doing?” I go, “What’s the problem?” He goes, “Those reviews were awful.”

ctx.x: There are times where an editor will say, or I’ll say if it comes up to me, I end up being the ombudsman for the company. You know people can’t decide what to do with things or there’s an argument whether we should do this or do that, the editors will come to me with that kind of problem and then we’ll work out a solution. But yeah, if we think the writer is being unfair, and there are times where it slips through because it doesn’t seem that way to us, and then later on I’ll go yeah, right, if the artist comes —…

then I’ll say yeah you’re absolutely right. Arturo Sandoval one time, we did a double review of two records of his. One got two stars, one got four stars. And I went to see Arturo live. And he goes, “Frank, what are you doing?” I go, “What’s the problem?” He goes, “Those reviews were awful.” I go, “Arturo what are you talking about?” He goes, “The four star review, all you talked about were the negatives in the review. In the two star review you only talked about the song that he liked.” And I go, “Really?” And I…
Oh. A learning process all the time.
